knowledge:
- key_parameters: assay.names=A named vector mapping MCMC or edgeR outputs (e.g., phi, phi_Z, Z, c, pi, logfc, prob) to specific assay names or colData in the PhIPData object ;; beadsRR=Logical indicating whether to run a beads-only round robin to estimate false positive rates ;; prior.params=List of prior parameters for the Bayesian model, including shape parameters for beta and gamma distributions (a_pi, b_pi, a_phi, b_phi, a_c, b_c, fc, a_0j, b_0j) ;; se.params=Parameters controlling the identification of super-enriched peptides (default fold-change threshold is 15) to exclude them from MCMC for speed ;; jags.params=List of MCMC parameters (e.g., n.chains, n.iter) passed directly to rjags ;; BPPARAM=A BiocParallelParam object (e.g., SerialParam(), SnowParam()) to control parallelization
- alternatives: edgeR (via runEdgeR)=Fast and effective at identifying highly enriched peptides, but less sensitive for peptides in the lower fold-change range compared to BEER ;; BEER (via brew)=Highly sensitive for lower fold-change ranges, but computationally intensive and takes much longer to run
- when_to_use: Appropriate for analyzing PhIP-seq data to identify enriched antibody responses by comparing serum samples against beads-only control samples.
- pitfalls: MCMC sampler may get stuck if beta shape parameters (a_0j, b_0j) are less than one; it is safer to ensure they are greater than one ;; MCMC parameter indices (e.g., Z[5, 1]) do not directly correspond to the row index of the PhIPData object because super-enriched peptides are removed prior to running MCMC ;; Inference can be very poor if there are too few beads-only samples or very few peptides.

workflows.name: phip_seq_enrichment
workflows.intent: Identify enriched antibody responses to peptides in PhIP-seq data using edgeR and Bayesian (BEER) modeling.
input: PhIPData object (containing PhIP-seq read counts for serum and beads-only samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Run edgeR to estimate peptide-specific dispersion and identify differentially expressed peptides ;; 2. Run BEER (Bayesian Estimation Enrichment in R) using brew() to obtain posterior probabilities of enrichment ;; 3. Identify enriched peptides (hits) by combining posterior probabilities and super-enriched peptides ;; 4. Run beads-only round robin using beadsRR() to estimate false positive rates ;; 5. Calculate expected reads/proportions using getExpected() and Bayes factors using getBF()
workflows.code:
edgeR_out <- runEdgeR(sim_data, 
                      assay.names = c(logfc = "edgeR_logfc",
                                      prob = "edgeR_logpval"))

assay(edgeR_out, "edgeR_hits") <- apply(
  assay(edgeR_out, "edgeR_logpval"), 2, 
  function(sample){
    pval <- 10^(-sample)
    p.adjust(pval, method = "BH") < 0.05
  })

assay_locations <- c(
  phi = "beer_fc_marg", 
  phi_Z = "beer_fc_cond", 
  Z = "beer_prob", 
  c = "sampleInfo", 
  pi = "sampleInfo"
)

beer_out <- brew(edgeR_out, assay.names = assay_locations)

was_run <- matrix(rep(beer_out$group != "beads", each = nrow(beer_out)), 
                  nrow = nrow(beer_out))

are_se <- was_run & is.na(assay(beer_out, "beer_prob"))

assay(beer_out, "beer_hits") <- assay(beer_out, "beer_prob") > 0.5 | are_se

edgeR_beadsRR <- runEdgeR(sim_data, beadsRR = TRUE, 
                          assay.names = c(logfc = "edgeR_logfc", 
                                          prob = "edgeR_logpval"))

beer_beadsRR <- brew(edgeR_beadsRR, beadsRR = TRUE, 
                     assay.names = assay_locations)

edgeR_beadsRR <- beadsRR(sim_data, method = "edgeR", 
                         assay.names = c(logfc = "edgeR_logfc", 
                                         prob = "edgeR_logpval"))

beer_beadsRR <- beadsRR(edgeR_beadsRR, method = "beer",
                        assay.names = assay_locations)

getExpected(sim_data)

brew(sim_data, beadsRR = TRUE) %>%
getBF()
